 Zach Bachar Nov 18, 2026 Led by Cooper Flagg's 33-point performance, the Dallas Mavericks took down the Golden State Warriors by the final score of 116-94 at the American Airlines Center on Wednesday.
 The Mavericks emerged victorious after heading into the game as 4.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

 Bleacher Report 1d Golden State suffered its fourth straight loss as star point guard Stephen Curry remains sidelined with an oblique abdominal tear .

 Golden State's offense continued to struggle without Curry, as Dallas began the game on a 25-9 run.
 The Warriors started to gain some momentum by cutting the deficit to 10 at the end of the first quarter before pulling to within six points early in the second.
 Dallas quickly responded with a 12-5 run to gain another double-digit advantage, however. 
 Both teams traded baskets throughout the remainder of the first half, as the Mavericks held a 62-49 advantage at halftime.
 Dallas gained more separation over Golden State as soon as the second half started, beginning the third quarter on an 18-4 run to take a 27-point lead.
 The Warriors were ultimately unable to chip away at the large deficit, as the Mavericks led by at least 18 points throughout the entire fourth quarter.
 Dallas' lineup was efficient offensively during the win, ending the game with 50.6/41.5/78.9 shooting splits as a team.
 The Mavericks and Warriors now own identical 8-7 records following Wednesday's result.
